title: Mackenzie data gave no clear annual-to-spring flow timing gap trend in 38 approved years from 1980 to 2019
abstract: We tested whether the annual flow midpoint moved later relative to the April-July flow midpoint at the Mackenzie Arctic Red River gauge. ArcticGRO v20261104 gave 38 complete approved years in 1980-2019; 1997 and 1998 were excluded without gap filling. The annual-minus-spring gap slope was +0.78 days per decade. Its conditional 95% five-position residual block limits were -0.39 to +1.94. All nine planned checks also had limits that included zero. Thus this separate basin and agency test gave no clear support for transfer of the published Yenisey gap result. It does not establish no change or a difference between rivers. A later-season flow share test was also uncertain. Short records, two missing years, seasonal windows, storage and regulation, source error and conditional uncertainty limit inference. The package gives original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit. Source records and year-level tables remain external.

display.caption: Annual and April-July flow midpoints at Mackenzie, with linear trends. Right: slopes and conditional 95% five-position block limits in 38 approved complete years from 1980 to 2019. The annual-minus-spring trend is uncertain.
